scope: Research only; game tracked files and dependencies unchanged. Real source evaluation in Chromium module Workers served from ordinary local static HTTP without COOP/COEP.
conclusion: Python, Lua and SQLite SQL can use existing real browser runtimes; no custom imitation parser/evaluator is needed for the existing generated exercises.

environment.note: Local loopback gzip server. Transfer and timing are environment measurements, not user Internet speed.

measurementCaveats: Timing is one local loopback sample, not Internet download time or a mobile-device benchmark.
loadMs begins after the worker statically imports the small JS entry module; it includes WASM load/initialization, not all worker creation overhead.
cold transfer bytes are gzip body lengths served by our test HTTP server; production CDN compression may differ.
warm is a fresh Worker in the same browser context using immutable HTTP cache. Zero HTTP requests were received by our local server; VM initialization still runs.
The runtime is loaded on demand per selected language, not all three on initial game load.

integrationRequirement.reproduced: Wasmoon1.16.0 doString calls retain return/error values on the Lua stack. Repeated calls without restoring the stack eventually returned _ENV=nil near lesson38 and memory access out of bounds. Closing the poisoned state also trapped.
integrationRequirement.resolutionVerified: Both doStringSync and async doString pass all1024 generated exercises when the wrapper saves/restores the Lua stack around every evaluation. Sync version is used by the main proof.

implementationShape.python: Self-host minimal Pyodide files; fresh isolated Worker per submission/session, compile()/exec() submitted source in an explicit namespace, run fixture assertions, destroy on timeout.
implementationShape.lua: Self-host Wasmoon index.js/glue.wasm; use doStringSync inside Worker, restore Lua stack after every call and isolate/reset state between submissions. Stack restoration also makes the asynchronous doString path pass all1024 tests; do not retain arbitrary return/error stack values between evaluations.
implementationShape.sql: Self-host official SQLite index.mjs/sqlite3.wasm; use :memory: DB, initialize test tables, execute user statement, compare result rows/database state. No OPFS persistence required; save progress in existing game JSON.
